Here's a draft of both sections. I've had to assume a few things, which are listed at the end. Put your real numbers in where you see brackets.

---

## Use of Funds

**$3M to reach Series A milestones over ~24 months of runway**

| Category | % | Amount | What it buys |
|---|---|---|---|
| Product & Engineering | 40% | $1.2M | 4 hires (3 engineers, 1 product designer); enterprise-readiness features (SSO, permissions, audit logs, key integrations) |
| Sales & Marketing | 35% | $1.05M | First 2 AEs, 1 SDR, demand gen and content program |
| Customer Success | 10% | $300K | 1–2 CS hires to drive onboarding, retention, and expansion |
| G&A & Compliance | 10% | $300K | SOC 2, legal, finance/accounting, tooling |
| Reserve | 5% | $150K | Buffer for delayed hires or longer sales cycles |

**Team: 6 → ~15 by month 18**

**Why this split:** Customers already pay us: we're at $40K MRR and growing 10% month over month, mostly through founder-led selling. This round turns that into a go-to-market engine we can repeat without the founders on every deal, and it keeps the product ahead of what larger customers need. About 75% of the money goes straight into building and selling.

**Runway:** We plan an average net burn of about $125K/month, which gives about 24 months of runway. Growing revenue offsets the cost of the hiring ramp. That leaves 6+ months of cushion to raise a Series A from a position of strength.

---

## Milestones

**Where this round gets us: ready for a Series A at ~$2M ARR**

| Timeline | Revenue | Key milestones |
|---|---|---|
| **Today** | $40K MRR ($480K ARR) | 6-person team, founder-led sales, 10% MoM growth |
| **Month 6** | ~$70K MRR | First AEs hired and ramping; SOC 2 Type I complete; [X] new logos |
| **Month 12** | ~$110K MRR (~$1.3M ARR) | Sales playbook is repeatable: AEs hit quota without founder involvement; first mid-market/enterprise contracts; SOC 2 Type II underway |
| **Month 18** | ~$165K MRR (~$2M ARR) | Series A metrics in hand; team of ~15; begin Series A raise |

**Efficiency targets we'll hold ourselves to by month 18:**
- Net revenue retention: >110%
- Gross margin: >75%
- CAC payback: <18 months
- Logo churn: <[X]% monthly
- Burn multiple: <2x

**How we get there:** [One line on your main growth levers, e.g., Move from founder-led sales to a 2-AE team, expand into [adjacent segment], and launch [key feature/integration] that opens up larger accounts.]

---

### Notes on the assumptions

- **Growth slows in the plan on purpose.** The projections assume 10% MoM for the first ~6 months, then 7–8% as the base grows. If you held 10% for 18 months you'd be at about $220K MRR. That would be great, but investors trust a plan that slows the way real companies do. You can show the 10% case as upside.
- **Burn is an estimate.** I don't know your current burn or salaries. Rebuild the runway figure from your actual hiring plan (fully loaded cost per hire × start month). The deck has to match your financial model exactly, because investors will check.
- **Tie every dollar to a milestone.** If an investor questions a line item, you should be able to name the milestone it pays for. For example, the CS hire protects NRR, and SOC 2 removes a blocker on enterprise deals.
- **Use your own specifics.** Fill in the brackets and adjust the hiring mix to fix your real bottlenecks. If you sell self-serve, move money from AEs toward growth marketing and product-led onboarding.
- **Slide tip:** On the slide itself, a simple pie or bar chart for use of funds and a 3–4 step milestone timeline work best. Keep the detailed tables for the appendix or your talking points.
fr-d2:
Here's a draft. Fill in the brackets with your real figures. Specific numbers are what make an honest update believable.

---

**Subject:** Q[X] update: we missed our revenue target, and signed two enterprise pilots

Hi everyone,

I'll start with the hard part: we missed our Q[X] revenue target by 30%. We brought in $[X] against a goal of $[Y]. Below I explain why it happened, what we're changing, and the progress that makes me confident about the next two quarters.

**The numbers**
- Revenue: $[X] vs. $[Y] target (−30%)
- MRR: $[X] ([+/−X]% vs. last quarter)
- Customers: [X] total ([+X] new, [X] churned)
- Cash: $[X] | Net burn: $[X]/month | Runway: [X] months

**Why we missed**
[Change these to what actually happened. Common examples:]
- **Deals slipped.** [X] deals we expected to close this quarter moved into next quarter. In most cases security and procurement reviews took longer than we expected.
- **Our forecast was too optimistic.** We counted deals in the pipeline that were still too early to rely on. That's on me, and I've changed how we forecast (see below).
- **[Other factor, e.g., a new hire took longer to ramp than planned, or a marketing channel underperformed].**

**What went well**
We signed two enterprise pilots:
- **[Company A]**: [brief description, e.g., Fortune 500 logistics company]. [X]-week pilot, [paid at $X / unpaid], focused on [use case].
- **[Company B]**: [brief description]. [X]-week pilot, [terms].

To be clear, these pilots aren't revenue yet. Both have agreed success criteria, and if they convert they would become annual contracts worth roughly $[X] combined. They also show that we can sell into larger organizations, which raises how big this business can get.

**What we're changing**
- **Forecasting:** Only deals at [stage, e.g., verbal commit or in procurement] count toward the quarter.
- **Focus:** [e.g., Putting our effort into converting both pilots, with one person responsible for each.]
- **Spend:** [e.g., Holding off on the X hire until we see pilot results, which extends runway to X months.]

**Goals for next quarter**
- Convert at least one pilot to a paid annual contract
- Revenue of $[X]
- [Third goal]

**Where you can help**
- Intros to [role, e.g., VP of Operations] at [type of company]
- Advice from anyone who's been through enterprise procurement or security reviews. 20 minutes would help a lot.
- [Any other specific ask]

I'd rather give you the full picture than a polished one. If you want to dig into anything, reply here or book time with me: [link].

Thanks for backing us,
[Name]

---

**A few notes:**
- **Lead with the miss.** If you bury it under the good news, you lose more trust than the miss itself would cost you.
- **Don't oversell the pilots.** Call them pilots, not wins or revenue. If they convert, your next update will be more believable.
- **Only give reasons you can back up.** If the honest reason is "we got the forecast wrong," saying so builds more credibility than blaming the market.
- **Make the asks specific.** Angels want to help, but they tend to ignore vague asks.
